Build an interactive 2D figure from the brief below and the source image.

AUTHORED FIGURE BRIEF:
This figure is a three-part illustration of a bouncing light pulse seen from two reference frames. Part (a) shows a side view of a space shuttle above a magnified inset: inside a rounded frame an astronaut in an orange suit, labeled Astronaut, floats beside an analog clock reading delta tau, while a Light source drawn as a yellow burst and a Receiver sit side by side beneath a Mirror, with teal arrows carrying the pulse straight up and straight back down over the bracketed vertical distance D. Part (b) shows the same apparatus from outside: three dashed-outline snapshots of the cabin run left to right, and a purple path labeled s goes diagonally up from the source in the left snapshot, labeled Beginning event, to the mirror in the middle snapshot, then down as a second segment s to the receiver in the right snapshot, labeled Ending event. Brackets below give the horizontal shifts L = v delta t / 2 and L, and a standing figure on a tan ground plane is labeled Observer on Earth beside a clock reading delta t. Part (c) reduces the picture to bare geometry, an isosceles triangle whose two slanted sides are each labeled s, divided by a vertical altitude D into right triangles with bases L = v delta t / 2 and L, with s = sqrt(D squared + L squared) written above. Drawing the same pair of events twice makes the two path lengths directly comparable, which is what forces the two recorded times apart.

REQUESTED INTERACTIONS:
- Toggle between astronaut frame and Earth frame: learner switches the named observer view; the light path changes from straight up-and-down distance 2D to two diagonal segments 2s while the clocks display delta tau and delta t; the frame dependence of elapsed time becomes clear.
- Slider for shuttle speed v: learner increases or decreases horizontal motion; the cabin snapshots spread apart, L grows, the diagonal light path lengthens, and delta t increases relative to delta tau; the geometric origin of time dilation becomes visible.
- Button sequence through beginning, mirror reflection, and ending event: learner steps the pulse through the three events; the same event markers light up in both apparatus and triangle panels; the shared events explain why the two observers can disagree about path length but not about what happened.

SOURCE FILE: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 38: Relativity

There is no blueprint: decide the figure type, elements, labels, controls, and any step sequence yourself.

Two frames, same two events. The astronaut sees the pulse go straight up & down (2D, time Δτ); the Earth observer sees it travel two diagonals (2s, time Δt). Switch frames and change v to see why Δt > Δτ.

var EVENT_NAMES = ['Beginning', 'Mirror reflection', 'Ending']; function halo(t) { return t.attr({ 'paint-order': 'stroke', stroke: '#fff', 'stroke-width': 3, 'stroke-linejoin': 'round' }); } function txt(parent, x, y, s, size, color, anchor) { return halo(parent.text(s).font({ size: size || 14, family: 'sans-serif', fill: color || '#111' }) .attr({ 'text-anchor': anchor || 'middle' }).move(x, y)); } function star(parent, cx, cy, r, color) { var pts = []; for (var i = 0; i < 16; i++) { var ang = Math.PI * i / 8, rad = (i % 2 === 0) ? r : r * 0.42; pts.push((cx + rad * Math.cos(ang)).toFixed(1) + ',' + (cy + rad * Math.sin(ang)).toFixed(1)); } return parent.polygon(pts.join(' ')).fill(color).stroke({ color: '#b8860b', width: 0.6 }); } function arrowHead(parent, x, y, angDeg, color) { var a = angDeg * Math.PI / 180, ux = Math.cos(a), uy = Math.sin(a), px = -uy, py = ux; var L = 13, W = 5, bx = x - ux * L, by = y - uy * L; var p = [x, y, bx + px * W, by + py * W, bx - px * W, by - py * W]; return parent.polygon(p.map(function (n) { return n.toFixed(1); }).join(' ')).fill(color); ast.rect(34, 50).radius(12).move(133, 262).fill('#e0703a').stroke({ color: '#7a3413', width: 1.5 }); ast.rect(12, 34).radius(6).move(120, 268).fill('#e0703a').stroke({ color: '#7a3413', width: 1.2 }); gA.line(96, 290, 128, 282).stroke({ color: '#333', width: 1 }); arrowHead(gA, 130, 281, -12, '#333'); // clock Δτ gA.circle(40).center(150, 372).fill('#fff').stroke({ color: '#333', width: 2 }); gA.line(150, 372, 150, 358).stroke({ color: '#c0392b', width: 2 }); gA.line(150, 372, 160, 372).stroke({ color: '#333', width: 2 }); txt(gA, 178, 366, 'Δτ', 15, '#111'); txt(gA, 210, 500, '(a)', 16, '#111'); var dynA = gA.group(); /* ---------- panel (b): Earth frame (static ground/observer) ---------- */ var gB = draw.group(); gB.polygon('500,470 920,470 965,512 470,512').fill('#d9cdb8'); // tan ground // observer figure gB.circle(16).center(700, 402).fill('#e8b48c').stroke({ color: '#333', width: 1 }); gB.rect(28, 40).radius(8).move(686, 412).fill('#7d9b52').stroke({ color: '#3c4d26', width: 1.2 }); gB.rect(11, 34).radius(4).move(689, 450).fill('#5b6b73').stroke({ color: '#333', width: 1 }); gB.rect(11, 34).radius(4).move(701, 450).fill('#5b6b73').stroke({ color: '#333', width: 1 }); txt(gB, 640, 470, 'Observer', 14, '#111', 'end'); txt(gB, 640, 486, 'on Earth', 14, '#111', 'end'); gB.line(645, 478, 678, 470).stroke({ color: '#333', width: 1 }); // observer clock Δt (face static, hand dynamic in dynB) gB.circle(40).center(760, 432).fill('#fff').stroke({ color: '#333', width: 2 }); txt(gB, 792, 428, 'Δt', 15, '#111'); txt(gB, 720, 540, '(b)', 16, '#111'); var dynB = gB.group(); /* ---------- panel (c): geometry triangle ---------- */ var gC = draw.group(); txt(gC, 500, 748, '(c)', 16, '#111'); Light speed is unchanged, so the Earth clock must read the larger Δt = ' + Dt.toFixed(2) + ' = γ·Δτ.'; } narr += ' Event: ' + EVENT_NAMES[state.step] + '.'; document.getElementById('demoNarration').textContent = narr; } /* ---------- controls ---------- */ window.update_v = function (val) { state.v = val; update(); }; window.setFrame = function (f) { state.frame = f; document.getElementById('frameAstronautBtn').classList.toggle('active', f === 'astronaut'); document.getElementById('frameEarthBtn').classList.toggle('active', f === 'earth'); update(); }; window.trigger_event = function () { state.step = (state.step + 1) % 3; update(); }; // hover tooltips on key panels gA.css('cursor', 'pointer').on('mousemove', function (e) { showTooltip('Astronaut (rest) frame: light path = 2D, elapsed time = Δτ (proper time).', e); }).on('mouseleave', hideTooltip); gB.css('cursor', 'pointer').on('mousemove', function (e) { showTooltip('Earth frame: moving cabin makes the light path two diagonals (2s); elapsed time = Δt = γΔt.', e); }).on('mouseleave', hideTooltip); gC.css('cursor', 'pointer').on('mousemove', function (e) { showTooltip('Geometry: each diagonal s = √(D² + L²) with L = vΔt/2. Since 2s = cΔt and 2D = cΔτ, this forces Δt = γΔτ.', e); }).on('mouseleave', hideTooltip); update(); window.__markRendered(); })(); // @FIGURE_CODE_END
